What it means: The Licensing Board for the City of Boston held a hearing regarding Little Haiti International Restaurant following an August shooting incident [00:23, 00:46, 01:04]. The board agreed by unanimous vote to reinstate the establishment's hours once it receives a security plan signed by police and staff training certificates [30:11, 30:20]. The board then voted on various premise inspection and transactional license matters [31:10, 37:53], approving several common victualler applications and managerial updates [55:20, 58:58] while rejecting an alcohol license application for Seven Hills Pasta Co without prejudice [53:43, 54:23].

Who moved it: George Cran presented the updated operational, seating, and security protocols for Little Haiti International Restaurant [02:06, 02:25, 08:59]. Attorney Green introduced the agenda items for the board's voting decisions [35:06, 36:17]. Board commissioners reviewed and voted on the applications, though the transcript does not settle all of their full names beyond brief mentions of Commissioner Honan, Commissioner Saxon, and the Chairman [11:34, 30:44].

What to watch: Watch for Little Haiti International Restaurant to submit its required security paperwork and staff training certificates to the board [30:11, 30:20], while observing a total capacity limit of 48 people including staff [30:27]. Seven Hills Pasta Co may utilize one-day licenses or reapply to the board in the future [53:43, 54:28]. The board noted that another violations conversation will occur moving forward [30:37], though the transcript does not settle specific future hearing dates for all rescheduled items [34:52, 34:55].

summary: The City of Boston Licensing Board held an informational hearing regarding Little Haiti International Restaurant [00:46] to review its security plan and operational updates following an August shooting incident [01:04], with the board voting unanimously to reinstate the establishment's license and hours once the official security plan signed by police and staff training certificates are submitted, keeping its total capacity strictly capped at 48 people including staff [30:11]. During the subsequent voting hearing on premise inspection violations, the board found no violation for Old Trafford Inc. [33:00] [33:20], Sophia's Food Enterprise Corp [35:26], and The Point LLC [37:25]. The board also reviewed and approved multiple transactional petitions and common victualler applications [38:09] [41:12] [48:40] [55:35], approved a new zip-code restricted license for Alcar LLC [54:39], and voted to deny Seven Hills Pasta Co's application for an on-premise alcohol license without prejudice [53:43].
